d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 4. The Temperate Region
d.notions: Temperate region, seasons, westerlies, Mediterranean climate, oceanic climate, continental climate.
d.focus: Location and types of temperate regions; characteristics of the temperate climate.
d.competence: Learners are able to explain why countries like France or England have four seasons and to prepare for a trip to a temperate country.
objectives: Locate the temperate regions of the world.
Name the four seasons of the temperate region.
Describe the three main types of temperate climate.
recall: Hot deserts lie between 15° and 30° north and south of the Equator.
People farm in the desert thanks to oases and irrigation.
Beyond the deserts, towards the poles, the climate becomes cooler.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: two countries between 30° and 60° north.
situation: Aïssatou's brother is going to study in France in January. He packs only T-shirts and sandals, as in Garoua.
His mother tells him that he will need a thick coat, gloves and closed shoes, because it is winter there. Her son does not understand why France is cold when Garoua is hot.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Aïssatou's brother does not understand why France is cold in January, while Garoua is hot.
What clothes does his mother advise him to take?
She advises him to take a thick coat, gloves and closed shoes.
What advice can you give to someone travelling to a temperate country?
He should check the season there before travelling and take clothes adapted to the cold or the heat.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the climate of the temperate countries, where many Cameroonians travel or study.

qa.q: Find the temperate regions on the map.
Look at the map. Between which latitudes are the temperate regions found?
qa.a: The temperate regions are found between about 30° and 60° north and south of the Equator, between the tropics and the polar regions.

qa.q: Name two temperate regions in the Northern Hemisphere and two in the Southern Hemisphere.
qa.a: In the north: Western Europe and the Prairies of North America. In the south: the Pampas of Argentina and New Zealand.

sum.title: I. Location
defs: The temperate region is the natural region found between about 30° and 60° north and south of the Equator, with neither very hot nor very cold climates.
items: Western Europe, the Mediterranean lands, the Steppes of Russia and Central Asia, and the Prairies of North America.
The Pampas of Argentina, the Veld of South Africa, southern Australia and New Zealand.

qa.q: In the temperate region, the year has four seasons. Name them.
qa.a: The four seasons are spring, summer, autumn and winter.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Which months are the warmest and the coldest in London? Does it rain every month?
qa.a: July is the warmest month (18.5°C) and January the coldest (5°C). Yes, it rains in every month, about 630 mm per year.

qa.q: Around the Mediterranean Sea, summers are hot and dry, while winters are mild and wet. What type of climate is this?
qa.a: This is the Mediterranean climate, found in Italy, Spain, Algeria, California and around Cape Town.

qa.q: In the centre of Russia and North America, far from the sea, summers are hot and winters are very cold. Why?
qa.a: These areas are far from the sea, which cannot moderate the temperatures. This is the continental climate.

sum.title: II. Types and Characteristics of the Climate
intro: The temperate region has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. There are three main types of temperate climate:
items: On western coasts between 45° and 60°, summers are mild, winters are cool, and it rains all year, as in London.
It is found on western coasts between 30° and 45°. Summers are hot and dry, and winters are mild and wet. Examples: Rome, Cape Town.
It is found in the interior of continents. Summers are hot, winters are very cold with snow, and rainfall is low. Examples: the Prairies, the Steppes.
The westerlies blow from the ocean and bring rain to the western coasts, especially in winter.

evaluation: Between which latitudes is the temperate region found?
The temperate region is found between about 30° and 60° north and south of the Equator.
Give two characteristics of the Mediterranean climate.
Summers are hot and dry, and winters are mild and wet.
Why are winters very cold in the centre of continents?
They are very cold because these areas are far from the sea, which cannot moderate the temperatures.
remediation: The temperate region lies between ______ and ______ north and south of the Equator.
The four seasons are spring, summer, ______ and winter.
The climate with hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters is the ______ climate.
London has a cool temperate ______ climate.
The winds that bring rain to western Europe are the ______.
The grasslands of North America are called the ______.
